6  Overview

Surprisingly, there appear to be very few randomized control trials that have specifically examined the use of BFR during ACL rehab, however a quick search revealed five different systematic reviews on the topic.

[1] included 4 studies and provides nice summaries of BFR protocols and results.

[2] concluded that short duration BFR intervention (13d) does not appear to measurably affect quadriceps CSA, thogh longer duration interventions appear to be more beneficial

[3] highlighted the sparseness and heterogeneity of the literature and suggested that future investigations with standardized protocols/outcomes, long term follow-up and more robust sample sizes are needed.

[4] included 8 studies and highlighted improvements in pain, IKDC score and isokinetic muscle strength, with variable outcomes for quadriceps volume and thickness.

[5] concluded that BFR after ACLR is safe and can aid in early quadriceps recovery when protocols employ individualized high occlusion pressures, low-load high-effort exercise, and moderate frequency.

7 Pre-Op Phase

Below is a summary of the protocols used in each of these studies. This information can be used to design safe BFR exercise programs in the pre-op phase.

  • Tramer et al 2023
  • Okoroha et al 2023
  • Kacin et al 2021
  • Zargi et al 2018

Exercises: [6]

  • Quadriceps contractions in end-range extension
  • Straight leg raises
  • Long arc quads
  • Double leg quarter squats

Limb Occlusion Pressure: 80%

Repetitions: 30-15-15-15

Intra-set Rest: 30 seconds

Inter-set Rest: 2 minutes

Sessions: 5x/week for 2 weeks

Notes: Exercises were chosen to work on volitional quad activation and knee extension ROM simultaneously.

Exercises [7]:

  • Quadriceps contractions in end-range extension
  • Straight leg raises
  • Long arc quads
  • Double leg quarter squats

Limb Occlusion Pressure: 80%

Repetitions: 30-15-15-15

Intra-set Rest: 30 seconds

Inter-set Rest: 2 minutes

Sessions: 5x/week for 2 weeks

Notes: Same as Tramer et al 2023 [6]

Exercises [8] :

  • Isotonic Leg Extension
  • Isotonic Leg Flexion

Limb Occlusion Pressure: 150mmHg

Repetitions: 2 rounds of 2 sets to failure

Load: 40RM

Intra-set Rest: 45 seconds

Inter-set Rest: 90 seconds

Sessions: 3x/week for 3 weeks

Notes: Criteria for inclusion - active knee extension deficit ≤ 5° and active flexion ≥ 120°

Exercises [9] :

  • Leg Extension

Limb Occlusion Pressure: 150mmHg

Repetitions: 3 rounds of 2 sets to failure

Load: 40RM

Intra-set Rest: 45 seconds

Inter-set Rest: 90 seconds

Sessions: 5 sessions over final 8 days pre-surgery

Notes: Criteria for inclusion - active knee extension deficit ≤ 5° and active flexion ≥ 120°

At this time, it appears that BFR in the pre-op phase is safe, although it’s effectiveness is yet to be determined by clinical trials. A CSI Pacific S&C coach who is experienced with implementing BFR may choose to include it as an addition to training in the pre-surgery phase once the athlete displays adequate ROM of ≤ 5° knee extension and ≥ 120° flexion.
